question.problem:
Consider the initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}-2y=f(x),\,y(1)=-4
$$

where $f(x)$ is a $2$-periodic function. Fill in the missing part in the solution of the IVP, where the infinite sum on the right-hand side below represents a particular solution ${y}_{p}$ of the differential equation.

*Hint: In this specific problem, the forcing function $f(x)$ is chosen such that the particular solution ${y}_{p}$ satisfies ${y}_{p}(1)=0.$*

The solution is 

$y(x)∼$   
{{field-1}} 
$+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }({a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x))$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of a linear differential equation of the form ${y}^{′}+P(x)y=f(x)$ is given by

$$
y={y}_{c}+{y}_{p},
$$

where ${y}_{c}$ is the general solution of the corresponding homogeneous equation, and ${y}_{p}$ is a particular solution.

First, we find the homogeneous solution. The general solution of ${y}^{′}-2y=0$ is 

$$
{y}_{c}=A{e}^{2x},
$$

where $A$ is an arbitrary constant.

Next, we identify the form of the general solution. Because the operator ${y}^{′}-2y$ involves a first derivative, a periodic forcing function $f(x)$ results in a particular solution containing both sine and cosine terms:

$$
y(x)∼A{e}^{2x}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }({a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x))
$$

Now, we apply the initial condition $y(1)=-4.$ Using the hint that the particular solution part evaluates to zero at $x=1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}y(1) & =A{e}^{2(1)}+{y}_{p}(1) \\ -4 & =A{e}^{2}+0 \\ A & =-4{e}^{-2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $A$ back into the homogeneous part:

$$
{y}_{c}=(-4{e}^{-2}){e}^{2x}=-4{e}^{2x-2}
$$

Therefore, the solution is

$$
y(x)∼-4{e}^{2x-2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }({a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x)).
$$
